content: 1. Denosumab has been shown to be superior to zoledronic acid in preventing skeletal-related events in patients with cancer. This conclusion is based on a combined analysis of three pivotal, randomized, phase 3 trials. (Lipton A, Fizazi K, Stopeck AT, et al., Eur J Cancer, 2012). 2. Radiation therapy plays a critical role in the management of bone metastases, providing effective pain relief and improving quality of life for patients. (De Felice F, Piccioli A, Musio D, et al., Oncotarget, 2017). 3. Studies comparing single-dose radiotherapy (e.g., 500 cGy or 800 cGy) with multi-fraction schedules (e.g., 300 cGy x 10 fractions) have demonstrated varying levels of efficacy in treating painful bone metastases. (Altundağ MB, Üçer AR, Çalıkoğlu T, et al., Onkol Derg, 2002). 4. A randomized clinical trial conducted in Iranian patients compared single versus multiple fractions of palliative radiotherapy for bone metastases, highlighting the effectiveness of both approaches in pain management. (Amouzegar-Hashemi F, Behrouzi H, Kazemian A, et al., Curr Oncol, 2008). 5. A prospective study conducted at Mansoura evaluated single-fraction versus multi-fraction radiotherapy for painful bone metastases, providing insights into the clinical outcomes of these treatment modalities. (Anter AH, Forum of Clinical Oncology, 2015). 6. A multicenter randomized study compared 20 Gy delivered in five fractions to 8 Gy delivered in a single fraction for palliative radiotherapy of bone metastases, demonstrating comparable efficacy in pain relief. (Badzio A, Senkus-Konefka E, Jereczek-Fossa BA, et al., Nowotwory Journal of Oncology, 2003). 7. A randomized trial conducted by the Bone Pain Trial Working Group compared 8 Gy single-fraction radiotherapy with a multi-fraction schedule over 12 months of follow-up, showing effective pain relief in metastatic skeletal pain. (Radiother Oncol, 1999). 8. A non-inferiority trial demonstrated that single-fraction radiotherapy is as effective as multiple fractions for repeat radiation in patients with painful bone metastases. (Chow E, van der Linden YM, Roos D, et al., Lancet Oncol, 2013). 9. A randomized clinical trial compared two palliative radiotherapy regimens (30 Gy in 10 fractions versus 8 Gy in a single fraction) for painful bone metastases, showing both regimens to be effective. (Foro Arnalot P, Fontanals AV, Galcerán JC, et al., Radiother Oncol, 2008). 10. Pain relief and quality of life improvements following radiotherapy for bone metastases were evaluated in a randomized trial comparing two fractionation schedules. (Gaze MN, Kelly CG, Kerr GR, et al., Radiother Oncol, 1997). 11. A randomized trial assessed the efficacy of radiotherapy in managing painful bone metastases, comparing single-dose and fractionated regimens. (Gutierrez Bayard L, Salas Buzon M del C, et al., Reports of Practical Oncology and Radiotherapy, 2014). 12. A study compared single-fraction radiotherapy with conventional fractionated radiotherapy for palliative treatment of painful bone metastases, demonstrating similar outcomes in pain relief. (Hamouda WE, Roshdy W, Teema M, Gulf J Oncol, 2007). 13. A randomized trial evaluated short-course versus long-course radiotherapy for palliative management of painful bone metastases, showing both approaches to be effective. (Hartsell WF, Scott CB, Bruner DW, et al., J Natl Cancer Inst, 2005). 14. A preliminary report from a randomized trial compared single and multi-fraction radiotherapy for bone metastases, providing early evidence of efficacy. (Kagei K, Suzuki K, Shirato H, et al., Gan No Rinsho Japan Journal of Cancer Clinics, 1990). 15. A prospective study investigated the effects of different fractionation schedules (10 x 3 Gy vs. 1 x 8 Gy) on pain relief and remineralization in bone metastases. (Koswig S, Budach V, Strahlentherapie und Onkologie, 1999). 16. A randomized trial compared single-dose versus fractionated palliative radiotherapy for bone metastases, demonstrating effective pain relief with both approaches. (Nielsen OS, Bentzen SM, Sandberg E, et al., Radiother Oncol, 1998). 17. A prospective randomized trial evaluated single and multi-fraction radiotherapy schedules for painful bony metastases, providing evidence for their clinical utility. (Price P, Hoskin PJ, Easton D, et al., Radiother Oncol, 1986). 18. A multicenter randomized trial compared short-course and long-course radiotherapy for palliative treatment of bone metastases, showing comparable efficacy. (Roos DE, Turner SL, O’Brien PC, et al., Radiother Oncol, 2005). 19. A prospective study compared multiple and single-fraction palliative radiotherapy for bone secondaries, highlighting the effectiveness of both approaches. (Sarkar SK, Sarkar S, Pahari B, et al., Indian J Radiol Imaging, 2002). 20. Further analysis of the Dutch Bone Metastasis Study confirmed the efficacy of single-fraction radiotherapy, even when accounting for retreatment. (van der Linden YM, Lok JJ, Steenland E, et al., Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys, 2004). 21. A randomized trial compared single-treatment radiotherapy with conventional fractionation for palliative management of painful bone metastases, demonstrating similar outcomes. (Cole DJ, Clin Oncol, 1989). 22. A randomized prospective trial compared three schedules of palliative radiotherapy, providing preliminary results on their effectiveness. (Foro P, Algara M, Reig A, et al., Oncologia, 1998). 23. The WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of pharmacological and radiotherapeutic management of cancer pain in adults and adolescents, advocating for evidence-based approaches tailored to individual patient needs. 24. The Dutch Bone Metastasis Study demonstrated the efficacy of radiotherapy for painful bone metastases during the last 12 weeks of life, providing valuable insights into end-of-life care. (Meeuse JJ, van der Linden YM, et al., Cancer, 2010). 25. A randomized trial compared three fractionation schedules for palliative radiotherapy in bone metastases, showing effective pain relief with all regimens. (Özsaran Z, Yalman D, et al., Strahlentherapie und Onkologie, 2001). 26. A clinical and biological assessment of single versus multiple fractions of palliative radiotherapy for bone metastases demonstrated comparable outcomes. (Safwat E, El-Nahas T, et al., J Egypt Natl Canc Inst, 2007). 27. A global analysis of the Dutch Bone Metastasis Study compared single-fraction and multi-fraction radiotherapy for painful bone metastases, confirming their efficacy. (Steenland E, Leer JW, et al., Radiother Oncol, 1999). 28. A comparative study evaluated single-fraction versus multi-fraction radiotherapy for bone metastases in prostate cancer patients, demonstrating similar effectiveness. (Yoon F, Morton GC, Cancer Manag Res, 2014). 29. The use of (18)F-fluoride PET-CT has been shown to facilitate early treatment of painful bone metastases with Sm-153 EDTMP, improving patient outcomes. (Storto G, Gallicchio R, et al., Nucl Med Biol, 2013). 30. The alpha-emitter radium-223 has been shown to improve survival in patients with metastatic prostate cancer. (Parker C, Nilsson S, et al., N Engl J Med, 2013). 31. The CONSORT 2010 guidelines provide updated recommendations for reporting randomized trials, ensuring transparency and reproducibility in clinical research. (Moher D, Hopewell S, et al., J Clin Epidemiol, 2010).
